title: Holy Week at home
hookLine: keep the days quiet and go to the Triduum
tomorrow: forty days of fasting. so why fifty days of feasting?

lines: THEY WATCHED WHERE HE WAS LAID.
cards: Friday, late afternoon. The body has been taken down and laid in a tomb cut out of rock. Luke follows a few women who came with Jesus from Galilee.
They watched where he was laid. They go home as the Sabbath draws on.
And then Luke writes a very quiet line, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "And returning, they prepared spices and ointments; and on the sabbath day they rested, according to the commandment."

teach.h: THE TRIDUUM: THREE DAYS AS ONE.
teach.b: They rested. Grief in their hands, spices ready, and they keep the Sabbath anyway. The Saturday between the cross and the empty tomb gets one sentence in Luke, and no speeches, no miracles, nothing to do but wait.
That's the shape of the three days the Church calls the Triduum, kept as one celebration from Thursday evening to Easter Sunday.
Thursday evening, the Mass of the Lord's Supper: feet washed, the altar stripped bare afterward. Friday: the Passion read aloud, the cross venerated, Communion from the bread kept since Thursday.
Saturday: silence, the tabernacle empty, until the Easter Vigil begins in the dark with a new fire.
Here's something to tell a friend tonight: on Good Friday, by the Church's own rule, no Mass is celebrated at all.
The day is held open, the way the women's Saturday was. So what does Holy Week look like at home?
Keeping the days quiet. Less noise, fewer plans, the music off on Friday, dinner simple. And the three liturgies go on the calendar first, before anything else claims the time.
The women in Luke weren't doing nothing on that Saturday. They were waiting, with the spices ready by the door.

how: Catholics keep the Easter Triduum with the Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday evening, the Celebration of the Passion on Good Friday, and the Easter Vigil on Saturday night; some families keep those days quiet at home.

on Good Friday the Church celebrates no Mass: the Passion, the cross, Communion kept from Thursday.
Luke says the women rested on the Sabbath

games.q: it's the Sabbath after the burial, and you're with the women in Luke: spices ready, grief fresh. what do they do?
o: go to the tomb at once with the spices.
leave Jerusalem and head home to Galilee.
games.why: Luke says they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment. the tomb waits until the first day of the week.

practice: Turn off whatever's playing and listen for the quietest sound you can find: a fan, traffic far off, your own breathing. Stay with that one sound, the way Holy Saturday stays with one silence.
When your mind reaches for the next thing, let it come back to the sound.

wordCard.voice: Holy Week at home. Keeping the days quiet, with the three liturgies of the Triduum on the calendar first.

orig.note: Latin: a space of three days; the Church's name for Thursday evening to Easter Sunday.

carryVoice: Keep this: the three days, Thursday, Friday, and a Saturday of spices and rest. Until tomorrow.
